transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

I keep losing track of what I’m supposed to be working on and can’t seem to stay organized with all the tickets and follow-ups at my job. Ever since my company shifted to a high-volume, rapid-response model, I've been struggling to keep up, which recently led to a major mistake and a formal performance improvement plan. My supervisor actually suggested I get evaluated because they suspected an underlying attention issue.

Before your company changed to this high-volume work style, did you have similar problems with attention and organization earlier in life, like in school or in past jobs? Or did these difficulties mainly start after the recent work stress began?

While the recent changes at work really brought things to a head, these issues actually go back to my childhood. Back in elementary school, my teachers were always writing notes home about me daydreaming, blurting out answers, and never finishing worksheets. My parents still joke about how I could never sit still long enough to finish my homework without wandering off.

Do you also have excessive, hard-to-control worry about many different parts of life—like work, finances, health, or family—on most days for at least 6 months? If so, did that worry start before the recent problems at work?

No, I wouldn't say I have that kind of constant, uncontrollable worry about everything in my life. My stress really just comes from the frustration of struggling to stay focused, keep organized, and manage my daily tasks.
Besides work, do these attention and organization problems also affect other parts of your life, like managing chores, bills, appointments, or conversations? Can you give one or two examples?

Yes, they definitely affect my life outside of work, especially at home. My wife gets really frustrated with me because I’ll say I’ll pay a bill, call the plumber, or confirm an appointment, but then it completely vanishes from my head until a late fee or reminder email shows up.

Do you still often feel physically restless or act impulsively—like fidgeting, interrupting people, or making quick decisions without thinking—or are your symptoms mainly trouble with attention and organization? Which of those causes the biggest problems for you right now?

I definitely struggle with both; I’m constantly jiggling my leg during calls, feeling pent-up energy in meetings, and catching myself interrupting coworkers. However, the attention and organization difficulties are causing the biggest problems right now, as they've directly led to my performance plan at work and caused me to fall behind on bills and class assignments.
